Each column carries exactly TWO components - one spanning the top-to-middle gap and one spanning the middle-to-bottom gap - and each rail is broken by series components. A 2kohm resistor hangs off the middle rail at the far right down to the single GND symbol. 18 components, 10 nets.

JUDGEMENT CALLS (sites):
  - S21 (332,469), S22 (476,470), S23 (683,471), S24 (848,478) - the four places where a vertical column crosses the middle rail, all CRITICAL, all deg=4, all tracer default junction: JUNCTION, all four. I dumped the raw pixels at S21, S22 and S24 with inkmap. Every one is a bare plain X: a 4px vertical stroke and a 2-4px horizontal stroke whose union at the crossing is exactly 4 wide x 4-5 tall, i.e. NO thickening in either axis - there is no solder dot anywhere on this sheet - and NO semicircular hop and NO sideways jog. (The tracer's 'hop=5.7' at S24 is a gentle rightward lean of the vertical between y=458 and y=475 that never returns; a hop must come back, this one does not.) With no dot and no hop the brief's rule 2 applies: in this dataset the drafters mark a hop or jog when they mean 'not connected', so a bare crossing is a real junction. Rule 3 points the same way: this drafter uses no marking convention at all on this sheet, so an unmarked crossing carries no negative signal. The layout is the clincher - every one of the five columns holds exactly one component between the top and middle rails and exactly one between the middle and bottom rails, with the leads stopping neatly at the rails. That arrangement is the standard ladder/mesh and only makes sense if the middle rail is a node for each column. Consequence of the other reading (crossing at all four): the middle rail would degenerate into a bare series chain V-AC/I-DC -> C#8 -> L#7 -> R#11 -> GND with no taps at all, and each column would become an unloaded series diode pair between the top and bottom rails - not electrically impossible, but it would make the middle rail's five careful intersections a coincidence and would leave five 2-terminal orphan mid-column nets. Rejected.
  - S7 (472,290), S8 (681,288), S9 (337,294) CRITICAL: JUNCTION. All three crops show a clean T - the column's top lead terminates on the top rail and does not continue above it. 'Crossing' is not expressible at a deg-3 T; the only alternative, 'none', would float the top lead of zener #5 / diode #6 / zener #2 on a one-terminal net.
  - S20 (68,466) CRITICAL: JUNCTION. Clean T on the left edge: the V-AC bottom / I-DC top column continues straight down and the middle rail branches east. 'None' would cut the middle rail off from both sources.
  - S32 (685,673) CRITICAL and S33 (474,674): JUNCTION. Clean Ts - the bottom leads of diode #9 and zener #13 terminate on the bottom rail. (S33 only became relevant after the port fix on #13; its default is correct.)
  - S34 (326,679) CRITICAL, hop=3.6: JUNCTION. inkmap shows a plain cross with zero thickening; the 'vertical below' is just a ~16px pen overshoot past the rail, not a branch, so this is really a T. The reported hop is the overshoot, not a detour.
  - Non-critical sites S1, S2, S3, S11, S12, S13, S15, S16, S18, S26, S28, S29, S31, S35, S36, S37, S39, S40, S41, S42 were all inspected in the montages. Every one is a handwritten value caption ('5uH', '15uF', '8V', '1KHZ', '5V', '9uF', '4uF', '1uH', '1uF') crossing a wire or a component outline, or the internal ink of a zener/inductor symbol. None touches a component terminal after the port fixes; all left at defaults.

Re-bound t0 -> p3 (left plate, joining the bottom of I-DC #14) and t1 -> p0 (right plate, joining the bottom rail). Removed orphan nets n11 and n12.

CLASSES: all 18 symbols match their COCO classes as drawn. Worth recording: component #7 is drawn as an unmistakable 5-loop coil - stylistically identical to inductors #1 (5uH) and #15 (1uH) - but the drafter captioned it '4 uF'. I am keeping the class as Inductor because the class describes the drawn symbol and the symbol is a coil; the caption's unit is simply a slip of the pen. This is a caption error, NOT a class error, so no override was applied. Zeners #2, #5 and #13 all carry the bent-end cathode bar and are correctly Zener Diode; #3, #6, #9, #10, #12 are plain triangle-and-bar diodes.

TERMINAL ORDER: all 18 components are 2-terminal (or the 1-terminal GND), so per the brief the left->right / top->bottom default order was left untouched - it does not affect any metric. No 3-terminal parts on this sheet.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. All 28 gap bridges were reported netlist-neutral and were left alone. ERC clean: 18 components, 10 nets, every terminal assigned, every net has >=2 terminals, and the GND symbol sits on net '0' together with the bottom of the 2kohm resistor.
